Recommended audit design: record each comparison as executed/pass, executed/fail, skipped, or error; include skip reasons, compared-element counts, and nullable error statistics. A skipped check has no measured error; zero error requires an executed, nonempty comparison. Report coverage separately from pass rates. Freeze atol/rtol before evaluating outcomes, documenting dtype, backend, and justification; exploratory tolerance changes require separate reporting.

For singleton versus batched GRU execution, hold weights, input histories, initial hidden states, padding, and evaluation mode fixed; align corresponding outputs and hidden states. For left-padded histories, select the final nonpadding position. Check shapes and finiteness, then require every element to satisfy `abs(actual-reference) <= atol + rtol*abs(reference)`, consistently designating the reference. Record violation counts and maximum absolute error; a single global relative-error statistic cannot replace elementwise checks. PyTorch documents this comparison rule and warns that mathematically equivalent batched and sliced computations need not be bitwise identical. [Comparison documentation](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/testing.html), [numerical accuracy](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/main/notes/numerical_accuracy.html).

Repeat identical singleton and batched executions separately to measure within-configuration variation, with dropout disabled and hidden state reset. Log software/hardware versions and deterministic settings; deterministic-algorithm mode can expose unsupported nondeterministic operations. Compare both paths against float64 computations using the same weights and inputs converted before execution. Reduced discrepancies at higher precision support a numerical explanation; persistent batch-order dependence, indexing errors, or reference disagreements warrant semantic investigation. Repeatability alone does not establish correctness, and float64 is a diagnostic reference, not exact ground truth. These are audit recommendations inferred from PyTorch’s documented numerical limitations. [Deterministic algorithms](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/main/generated/torch.use_deterministic_algorithms.html).
